combo_label: At the Opticians × Falconry × The Canterbury Tales

entries.clue: Bend forward at the shoulders, and the falconer's word for a shut-winged dive
Herald's sleeveless overcoat, and the name of the inn where they set out
Holy tomb that draws the faithful; theirs stood behind the high altar
Somerset spa city; the much-wedded woman from beside it has buried five husbands
Wild adult hawk taken by trap, source of a word now meaning gaunt and worn
High street professional who tests your sight and fits your lenses
Covey game bird the dogs put up for a falcon circling over the stubble
Unhopped malt brew of the day; one rider is too full of it to wait his turn
Thomas, the archbishop struck down by four of the king's men in 1170
Faint wash of colour in a lens, taking the edge off bright light
Feathered dummy swung on a cord to fetch a falcon back down out of the sky
Sterile rinsing fluid, mild as tears, for flushing a lens clean
